# Project Plan {.unnumbered #sec-plan}

## Overview

This project extends a validated satellite-imagery-based crosswalk-geometry measurement methodology countywide across Cook County, Illinois, and links the resulting crossing-distance dataset to socioeconomic deprivation, pedestrian fatality, and crash-injury data to answer applied pedestrian-safety questions. Full background, literature review, and the study's research aims and working hypotheses are documented in [Background and Aims](phase00.html).

**Research aims:**

1. Produce a countywide crossing-distance dataset spanning Chicago community areas and suburban Cook County municipalities (~200 areal units), via two sub-aims:
   - **1a** — Compare three imagery/model approaches (3-band and 4-band Cook County orthoimagery, and Google Maps imagery — the original reference methodology's source) against manually measured ground truth on a sample of intersections, to determine which the countywide run should use. See [Crossing Distance Model Comparison](phase01_crosswalk_models.html).
   - **1b** — Produce the full countywide dataset using the approach Aim 1a supports.
2. Compare crossing distance across municipalities/community areas against socioeconomic deprivation (ADI) and demographic/employment covariates.
3. Relate crossing distance to point-level pedestrian fatalities (NHTSA FARS).
4. Model the areal rate of pedestrian crashes (IDOT crash records) as a function of median crossing distance, population density, median age, ADI, and other covariates identified in the literature.

## Project Structure

This book is the project's working plan. It is organized into five parts, one per phase, mirroring the structure of an academic paper. Each part contains the chapter(s) for that phase, and each chapter tracks its own tasks, data resources and status, so this page serves as the summary and the chapters hold the detail.

| Phase | Focus | Chapter(s) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Background, literature review, gaps in past research, study purpose, aims and hypotheses | [Background and Aims](phase00.html) | Complete |
| 1 | Dataset development: study area boundaries, intersections, streets, crashes, fatalities, ADI, census, and other contextual data | [Dataset Development](phase01.html); [Street Intersections](phase01_intersections.html); [Crossing Distance Model Comparison](phase01_crosswalk_models.html); [Appendix A: Data Preparation Code](dataprep.html) | In progress |
| 2 | Data presentation and analysis: descriptive statistics and statistical model specification/execution | [Data Presentation and Analysis](phase02.html) | Not started |
| 3 | Results, interpretation, and discussion of statistical tests | [Results and Discussion](phase03.html) | Not started |
| 4 | Study limitations, implications, conclusion, and next steps | [Limitations and Conclusions](phase04.html) | Not started |

| Data Analyst / Statistician & Quant Lead (Sufi) | Spatial and statistical modeling (Aims 2–4); ADI/demographic data assembly; crash and fatality data cleaning and merging; manual QA/validation sampling; municipal boundary reconciliation; literature review; general research assistance |

## Data Sources Summary

| Data | Source | Aim(s) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Study area geography (community areas + municipalities) | Chicago/Cook County health atlases | 1–4 | Complete |
| Street intersections | OpenStreetMap (Geofabrik extract) via osmium and OSMnx | 1, 3, 4 | Complete |
| Street network and speed limits | OpenStreetMap via Geofabrik/`osmextract` | 3, 4 | Complete |
| Traffic volume and vehicle mix (AADT, truck AADT) | Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT) | 3, 4 | In progress |
| Pedestrian fatalities | NHTSA FARS | 3 | Complete |
| Crash records | Illinois Department of Transportation (IDOT) | 4 | Complete |
| Area Deprivation Index (ADI) | Neighborhood Atlas (Univ. of Wisconsin) / ACS via `sociome`+`tidycensus` | 2 | Complete |
| Crossing-distance imagery (candidate A) | Google Maps satellite tiles (reference methodology's original source) | 1a, 1b | Not started |
| Crossing-distance imagery (candidate B) | Cook County 3-band RGB orthoimagery (leaf-off, single-vintage) | 1a, 1b | Not started |
| Crossing-distance imagery (candidate C) | Cook County 4-band RGB+NIR orthoimagery (leaf-off, single-vintage) | 1a, 1b | Not started |
| Crossing-distance segmentation pipeline | Fine-tuned SAM 2.1 + grow-cut (existing); channel-extended/re-fine-tuned variant for the 4-band candidate | 1a, 1b | Not started |

See [Dataset Development](phase01.html) for the detailed, task-level status of each data layer.

## Anticipated Outputs

1. Public/shareable Cook County crosswalk-distance dataset spanning Chicago community areas and suburban municipalities.
2. Manuscript: imagery source and segmentation model comparison for crossing-distance measurement — 3-band and 4-band Cook County orthoimagery vs. Google Maps imagery, validated against ground truth (Aim 1a). Designed to stand alone as a methods contribution, independent of Aims 2–4.
3. Manuscript: municipal/community-area crossing distance, ADI, and socioeconomic patterns across Cook County (Aim 2).
4. Manuscript: crossing distance and point-level pedestrian fatality risk using FARS (Aim 3).
5. Manuscript or technical report: crossing distance and crash-reported pedestrian injury rates across Cook County (Aim 4).
6. Updated open-source codebase reflecting the countywide pipeline, including the channel-extended segmentation model if Aim 1a supports the 4-band approach.
7. Interactive map/dashboard of Cook County crossing distances (optional, dissemination-stage).
